findings: TQ1_0/TQ2_0 quantizers are absmax ternary (d=max|w|, no Lloyd): fork ggml-quants.c quantize_row_tq1_0_ref; per-tensor cos 0.69 vs f16 (deployed Lloyd PQ2_0 ~0.90). PTQ1_0 = same rule at group 128 and ignores GGML_PQ2_0_LLOYD.
imatrix is a no-op for TQ1_0 (identical PPL to 4 dp with/without; TQ1_0/TQ2_0 yield identical weights, different packing -> identical PPL 1,860,827.3004).
Two independent runtimes (fork 0.2.0-dev build 10721; prism build 0.5.0-dev 11248) produce the same token-soup output from the TQ1_0 file, so this is codec quality, not a kernel bug.

Q2_K (+imatrix, non-ternary, 3.56 GiB) runs on both builds and beats the QAT artifact on PPL (13.0553 vs 23.2508), generation (clean vs math loop), and size (3.56 vs 5.52 GiB); mainline-compatible, no fork metadata.
The QAT artifact's generation blocker reproduces under the fixed-seed harness: math probe answers 120 km/h then loops '1. 1. 1...' (repeat 8-gram frac 0.846).
decision: No release. The QAT pipeline clearly beats every plain ternary codec (TQ1_0/TQ2_0/PTQ1_0 are BitNet-oriented absmax codecs and collapse to 1.9-2.1M PPL + token soup on this f16 model), but it does not clear the real bar (trained-low-bit Bonsai ~1.44x; plain Q2_K here at 1.04x) and its free generation is degenerate. Proposed (needs approval): one proper QAT run (mixed corpus incl. code/math, 5-10M tokens, hidden + top-k logits KD, ~$8-15) accepted on clean generation on this suite, PPL <= ~18, and KL/top-1 vs bf16 on ~250k mixed tokens before any HF upload.
